full_judgment:
Md Nazrul Islam Talukder, J: On an application under section 10(1A) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 along with section 439 read with section 435 Code of Criminal Procedure, this Rule at the instance of the accused-petitioner, was issued calling upon the opposite-parties to show cause as to why the order dated 30-9-2019 passed by the learned Senior Special Judge, Cox's Bazar in Criminal Petition Case No.19 of 2019 under section 419/465/409/ 467/468/471/34 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947, should not be set-aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The prosecution case, in short, is that the present petitioner being complainant filed CR Case No. 19 of 2019 before the Court of learned Senior Special Judge, Cox's Bazar under sections 419/465/409/467/468/471/34 of the Penal Code, 1860 with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 against the accused-opposite parties stating, inter-alia that the government acquired 73 acre of land of BS dag Nos. 293 and 295 corresponding to BS Khatian No. 128 under Mouza Chiringa, Cox's Bazar. On Golam Kader, Ahmed Hossain, Gul Cheher, Gul Nahar and Mazeda Khatun were the owner of the said land and their names were recorded and published in BS Khatian No. 128 of Mouza Chiringa, Cox's Bazar. The BS tenant Gul Cheher sold out her share of land to Golam Kader and Ahmed Hossain, the father of complainant by way of registered deed No.2000 dated 2-5-1987. After the death of the father of the complainant, the complainant and witnesses inherited the property and got possession of the scheduled land. The aforesaid land was acquired by the government and LA section of the office of the deputy commissioner issued notice upon the complainant and witnesses of the instant case for taking compensation. But the accused-opposite parties took away the award money of the complainant and witnesses of the instant case by practicing fraud and corruption upon the office of the Deputy Commissioner and the complainant-petitioner and the witnesses of the case. Hence, the petition of complaint. 

 13. He then submits that this revisional application under section 10(1A) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 does not lie before this court for the reasons that firstly, the impugned order is not an order under section 200 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, secondly, filing of a complaint case under section 200 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for ACC cases is unavailable and thirdly, rule 3(2) and rule 13(3) of the Anti-Corruption Commission Rules, 2007 and section 10(1A) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 were not complied with while filing of petition of complaint directly in the court and, as such, there is no illegality apparent on the face of the record causing miscarriage of justice and, as such, the Rule is liable to be discharged. 

 14. He lastly submits that the complainant should have submitted the complaint before the Anti-Corruption Commission and then collected a receipt thereof under Rule 3(2) of the ACC Rules. 2007 and then a letter from ACC showing its decision not to proceed with the application and then the said !encr become the pass for the complainant to file the petition of complaint directly before the court under Rule 13(3) of the ACC Rules, 2007 and if the court refuses to accept the petition of complaint, in that case, the complainant under section 10(1A) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 may prefer a revisional application before this court but the Rules were not complied with and considering all the legal aspects of the case, this Rule is liable to be discharged. 

 20. From the aforesaid mandate of law, it is crystal clear that if anybody is aggrieved by any schedule offence of the ACC Act, 2004, the complainant should have submitted the complaint disclosing all the facts and allegations to the Anti-Corruption Commission and collected receipt thereof under Rule 3(2) of the ACC Rules, 2007 and then a letter from the ACC containing its decision not to proceed with the complaint. If the complaint is aggrieved by any decision of the ACC, he then may file a petition of complaint directly before the court under Rule 13(3) of the ACC Rules, 2007 and if the complainant is dissatisfied with the decision of the court, he then may approach this court under section 10(1A) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958.
